text:
For **new-build select-service hotels in the Caribbean and Latin America (CALA)**, the brands most often included in an initial development shortlist are:

| Parent company | Commonly considered brands | Typical positioning/use |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | **Courtyard by Marriott**, **Fairfield by Marriott**, **Four Points by Sheraton**, **City Express by Marriott** | Courtyard and Four Points for upscale business/airport locations; Fairfield for upper-midscale projects; City Express for efficient midscale development, especially in Mexico and secondary Latin American cities. Marriott formally classifies these within its select-service portfolio, and City Express is marketed specifically for development throughout CALA. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/select-brands)) |
| **Hilton** | **Hilton Garden Inn**, **Hampton by Hilton**, **Tru by Hilton** | HGI for upscale select service; Hampton for upper-midscale; Tru for compact, value-oriented projects. Hilton entered 2026 with more than 90 focused-service hotels in its CALA pipeline and region-specific Hampton and Tru prototypes. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hilton-ends-2025-with-robust-luxury-and-lifestyle-growth-across-the-caribbean-and-latin-america)) |
| **IHG Hotels & Resorts** | **Holiday Inn Express**, **avid hotels** | Holiday Inn Express is one of the region’s most established limited-service flags; avid is a newer, lower-cost midscale option, currently gaining traction particularly in Mexico. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-strengthens-position-across-mexico-latin-america-and-the-caribbean)) |
| **Hyatt** | **Hyatt Place**; **Hyatt House** when extended stay is relevant | Hyatt Place is the principal upscale select-service option. Hyatt House is usually considered for projects with meaningful corporate, relocation or longer-stay demand. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Accor** | **ibis**, **ibis Styles**, occasionally **ibis budget** | Particularly important in Brazil, the Southern Cone and selected Andean markets. ibis is a standardized economy product; ibis Styles provides a more design-oriented alternative. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/midscale-economy-brands-novotel-mercure-ibis?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Wyndham Hotels & Resorts** | **La Quinta by Wyndham**, **Wyndham Garden**, **TRYP by Wyndham**, **Microtel by Wyndham** | La Quinta and Wyndham Garden serve upper-midscale demand; TRYP fits urban lifestyle locations; Microtel can suit highly cost-sensitive secondary markets. La Quinta is explicitly offered for new construction in Latin America. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/brand/la-quinta/?utm_source=openai)) |

### Most typical “core” competitive set

For a conventional **100–180-room urban, airport or commercial-corridor new build**, the first-round shortlist frequently narrows to:

- Courtyard by Marriott  
- Fairfield by Marriott  
- Hilton Garden Inn  
- Hampton by Hilton  
- Holiday Inn Express  
- Hyatt Place  
- City Express by Marriott  
- ibis or ibis Styles  
- La Quinta or Wyndham Garden  

### More situational options

- **Lifestyle/urban:** AC Hotels, Aloft, Moxy, TRYP or Caption by Hyatt  
- **Extended stay:** Hyatt House, Home2 Suites, Residence Inn, Staybridge Suites or Candlewood Suites  
- **Lower-cost midscale:** avid, Tru, City Express, Microtel or ibis budget  
- **Conversion-oriented brands:** Spark by Hilton, Garner and some soft brands may enter the discussion, but they are generally less natural starting points for a purpose-built new-build project.

Brand fit varies considerably by country. **Mexico has the broadest franchise competition; Accor tends to be more influential in Brazil; and Caribbean projects often favor globally recognized reservation systems and brands with proven airport, business and mixed leisure demand.** A regional developer profiled in 2026, for example, reported a portfolio dominated by Marriott and Hyatt select-service hotels across Costa Rica, Mexico, Jamaica and El Salvador. ([costar.com](https://www.costar.com/article/228571227/caribe-hospitality-sees-branded-select-service-hotels-as-path-forward-in-caribbean-and-latin-america))

The final shortlist should be tested against **territorial availability, key count, construction cost per room, food-and-beverage requirements, fee structure, loyalty contribution, management availability and projected rate premium** rather than brand recognition alone.
